title: TokTier: Exact Stateful CPU+GPU Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
event_hint: TokTier (ASU) introduces a stateful CPU+GPU tokenization service that guarantees byte-identical token IDs, cutting tokenization time so sharply that under a 50ms P99 objective 4 CPU cores + 1 GPU sustain 1,821 req/s where a 16-core stateless front end saturates at 40.
problem: LLM serving stacks cache prompt KV state but the front end still re-tokenizes the full request text on every call. For coding agents that append a small tool result to a long transcript, tokenization grows from 10% to 64% of time-to-first-token as the fleet prompt-cache hit rate approaches 0.99, because a short append can shift token boundaries near the end of the prior sequence.
mechanism: A two-mode stateful tokenization service enforcing one contract (emitted IDs always identical to full reference tokenization). For session continuations it keeps the prior token sequence, re-tokenizes a small window around the append, and splices only when a per-request check finds a stable pre-tokenization boundary (else widens or falls back). For calls without a reusable prefix it decomposes GPT-family regex pre-tokenization into run-local rules and runs exact pre-tokenization and BPE on a GPU. A sampled shadow verifier re-checks live traffic against the reference.

evidence.claim: Across 153,951 agent calls the median append is ~1.4K characters and only 1.0-3.6% of calls start or rebuild a session; at the fleet's 94.1% prompt-cache hit rate, as it approaches 0.99 tokenization grows from 10% to 64% of time to first token.
evidence.value: median append 1.4K chars; 1.0-3.6% session starts; tokenization 10%->64% of TTFT
evidence.condition: 153,951 calls from two agent ecosystems; component measurements at varying prompt-cache hit rates
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1 (Abstract): 'Across 153,951 calls ... the median call appends only about 1.4 K characters, and only 1.0-3.6% of calls start or re-build a session ... the aggregate prompt-cache hit rate is 94.1%, and as it approaches 0.99, tokenization grows from 10% to 64% of time to first token.'

evidence.claim: Incremental repair takes 0.5-1.1ms from 100K to 3M characters, up to 437x faster than HF tokenization and 2.1x faster at 1M characters than Gigatoken (the strongest cache-based baseline) in its most favorable, fully prewarmed mode; GPU full tokenization encodes 1M characters in 0.87ms, up to 491x below HF and 23.4x below the fastest published CPU method.
evidence.value: repair 0.5-1.1ms (437x vs HF; 2.1x vs Gigatoken); GPU 0.87ms @1M (491x vs HF; 23.4x vs fastest CPU)
evidence.baseline: HuggingFace tokenization; Gigatoken (cache-based, fully prewarmed); fastest published CPU method
evidence.condition: 17 production tokenizer families; 1.5x10^10 split checks; 12.4TB real-text corpus; 93,000+ replayed agent steps; zero divergence
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1 (Abstract): 'Incremental repair takes 0.5-1.1 ms from 100 K to 3 M characters, up to 437x faster than HF tokenization and 2.1x faster at 1 M characters than the strongest cache-based baseline (i.e., Gigatoken) ... GPU full tokenization encodes a 1 M-character request in 0.87 ms, up to 491x below HF tokenization and 23.4x below the fastest previously published CPU method.'

evidence.claim: With vLLM in the loop, TokTier lowers median time to first token by 16-34% in loaded regimes and P99 by 23% under recorded burst arrivals.
evidence.condition: Closed-loop sessions; e.g., 95K tokens/session improves median TTFT 23% with two back-to-back sessions, 16% with three, 34% with two sessions plus a two-second think time
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1 (Abstract): 'With vLLM in the loop, TokTier lowers median time to first token by 16-34% in loaded regimes and P99 by 23% under recorded burst arrivals.' See also PDF Page 14 (closed-loop experiments).

evidence.claim: Under a 50ms P99 objective, four repair cores plus one GPU sustain 1,821 requests/s, where a 16-core stateless CPU front end saturates at 40.
evidence.value: 1,821 req/s (4 cores + 1 GPU) vs 40 req/s (16-core stateless)
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1 (Abstract): 'Under a 50 ms P99 objective, a four-core repair pool plus one GPU sustains 1,821 requests/s, where a 16-core stateless CPU front end saturates at 40.'

evidence.claim: Per-request CPU time is 13.4ms for fastokens vs 2.3ms for TokTier repair and 0.15ms for GPU full tokenization; at 0.5 req/s per inference GPU this is 6.7 / 1.1 / 0.1 front-end CPU cores per 1,000 GPUs. Session token state costs ~16 bytes/token (a 500K-token session holds <15MB) vs gigabytes for the corresponding KV state.
evidence.value: 13.4ms vs 2.3ms vs 0.15ms per request; 6.7/1.1/0.1 cores per 1,000 GPUs; <15MB for 500K-token session
evidence.condition: 153,529 calls with complete token accounting (mean 117K tokens, mean hit 0.88); rate normalization at 0.5 req/s per inference GPU
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 23 (Table 8) and PDF Page 14 (Section 5.7 Cost and resource use): '13.4 ms of CPU time per request for fastokens and 2.3 ms for TokTier repair ... GPU full tokenization contributes 0.15 ms ... 6.7, 1.1, and 0.1 front-end CPU cores per 1,000 GPUs ... a growing 500 K-token session holds its resident footprint under 15 MB.'

evaluation_context: Workload: 153,951 calls from two agent ecosystems (SWE-smith streams under Qwen3, Llama 3.1, gpt-oss; plus public Codex trace). Hardware: GPU full tokenization benchmarked across RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000, GH200, H100 NVL, A100 (Table 9); repair measured with reference HF/Rust engines. Differential campaigns: 17 production tokenizer families, 1.5x10^10 split checks, 12.4TB real-text corpus, 93,000+ replayed agent steps, zero divergence. Closed-loop TTFT measured with vLLM at 95K tokens/session. Shadow verifier caught a history-dependent bug in a widely deployed production Rust tokenizer (39/40 sampled sessions diverged).
limitations: At four concurrent sessions the inference engine cannot retain the needed KV state and prefix reuse collapses (tokenization placement becomes irrelevant). For large appends (delta=100K chars, beyond P99 of 38K / the 0.8% of calls reaching 50K) the fully prewarmed cache leads repair at every context shape; three explored prototype routes (A: parallel repair; B: cache-based window engine) are exploration prototypes that have not passed the certification battery gating the shipped repair path. GPU is only ~1.5x better in tokens/watt than the best 32-core CPU config under an accounting that favors the CPU.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to cross-region / agent-cache infrastructure: tokenization is an overlooked front-end bottleneck that dominates TTFT once KV-cache reuse is saturated. TokTier's exactness contract (byte-identical IDs, certified-boundary splice) is what makes incremental token-state reuse safe alongside prefix-cache and KV-cache reuse, and its small per-session state (<15MB vs gigabytes for KV) makes token-state sharing across regions far cheaper than KV-state sharing.
source_notes: Primary source: arXiv:2607.29678v2, TokTier, Z. Zhang & Z. Cao, Arizona State University, 31 Jul 2026; document.fetch_status=FETCHED.

All headline numbers in the abstract are restated in the body with explicit baselines (HF, Gigatoken prewarmed, fastokens) and conditions (tokenizer family, context size, hardware) on PDF pages 1, 11, 14, and 23.
